title: Personal Loans Servicing Standard: Payment Acceptance, Interest Accrual and Allocation
content:
## Standard

Payments are accepted on a Personal Loans loan in active or charged-off status. Interest accrues daily as simple interest on the unpaid principal at the current interest rate, on an actual/365 basis: the interest accrued at a payment equals the unpaid principal times the current interest rate divided by 100 and by 365, times the number of days from the interest paid-through date to the payment's effective date (the effective date minus the paid-through date), rounded to the cent. Interest does not accrue on unpaid fees, and no interest accrues on a charged-off loan.

Each payment is applied in the order accrued interest, then unpaid fees (oldest fee first, each as its own fee payment line), then principal; after the payment the interest paid-through date is the effective date when the accrued interest was fully paid. An installment is treated as paid once the payment amounts credited toward it - counted in full, including any part applied to fees - reach the scheduled payment amount; each fully covered installment advances the next due date by one month on the due day, and a payment never covers more than the installments already due plus the next one. Any amount beyond that is applied to principal and does not advance the next due date.

A payment's effective date is the business day it was submitted when submitted by the same-day cutoff Eastern Time, otherwise the next business day; a mailed check is effective on the business day it is received; business days follow the Federal Reserve holiday calendar. A one-time payment must be at least the grade's one-time payment minimum unless it pays the loan off. A debit card payment is accepted only if it does not exceed the debit card maximum and fewer than the monthly maximum of debit card payments have posted on the loan in that calendar month. Payments taken by a representative by phone carry no fee. Balances and delinquency fields on the loan are refreshed after every payment, return, fee, fee payment and waiver.

The debit card count for a month takes every debit card payment posted on the loan with an effective date in that calendar month, returned ones included.

## Worked allocation (hypothetical figures)

A loan with 5000.00 USD of unpaid principal at 12.00 percent, paid through 1 March, receives a 450.00 USD payment effective 1 April, 31 days later, with 15.00 USD of unpaid fees:

| Step | Amount |
|---|---|
| accrued interest: 5000.00 times 12.00 divided by 100 and by 365, times 31 | 50.96 |
| to interest | 50.96 |
| to the unpaid fee | 15.00 |
| to principal | 384.04 |

The whole 450.00 counts toward the installment, fee part included.

## Debit card limits (hypothetical month)

| Debit card payments already posted this month | New card payment | Accepted |
|---|---|---|
| 2, one later returned | 300.00 | yes: 2 is fewer than 3 |
| 3 | 300.00 | no |
| 0 | 2600.00 | no: above the card maximum |
